title: Group and rank Personal Signals and pinned-MIT YEIS destinations in Universe Navigator

scope.subject: Navigator discovery, grouping and result ranking on the existing YEIS destination model

research_summary: Improve discovery without adding a second astronomy index. The pinned MIT YEIS Search/Places model remains the spatial and astronomical authority; Personal Universe only groups and ranks the already-resolved destinations. Personal Signals should remain first-class, browse should expose meaningful groups, and query ordering should prefer personal/exact/prefix matches while preserving existing keyboard Open/Locate behavior. cmdk+Fuse and Pagefind remain valid generic search options but would duplicate or bypass the domain indexes already restored from YEIS.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT YEIS already defines one keyboard-driven search surface over bodies, foreign-system bodies, catalogue stars, black holes, landmarks and galaxies; Personal Universe should preserve that domain authority while improving presentation.

cmdk provides a mature command-palette shell and keyboard navigation, while Fuse.js can add generic fuzzy ranking; using them as the astronomy index would duplicate the YEIS search model already integrated.
Pagefind is a strong static full-text search subsystem for documents and articles, but it does not model spatial universe destinations or YEIS navigation semantics.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep the selected pinned MIT YEIS product/search model as the full astronomical authority and improve only how its resolved destinations are grouped and ranked.
No additional framework is needed because the existing React shell already renders the navigator and YEIS supplies the domain queries.
Pagefind is valuable for future document search but is not a replacement for the current spatial destination subsystem.
cmdk/Fuse can supplement generic command-palette UX later, but current grouping/ranking can reuse the existing destination model without another dependency.

candidates.name: Existing Personal Universe Navigator over pinned MIT YEIS destinations
candidates.source: Current UniverseNavigator plus pinned MIT YEIS Search/Places destination model
candidates.license: MIT source at pinned e520568 plus project-owned React presentation
candidates.reason: Preserves one astronomy/search authority and requires only product-specific grouping and ranking over already-resolved destinations.

candidates.name: cmdk + Fuse.js command palette and fuzzy ranking
candidates.reason: Useful generic UX tooling but unnecessary for this bounded improvement; making Fuse authoritative would duplicate YEIS indexes and add a dependency without improving spatial semantics.

candidates.name: Pagefind static full-text search
candidates.reason: Strong for long-form document search but not for stars, worlds, galaxies, landmarks or native camera actions; it would sit beside rather than replace YEIS navigation.

decision.rationale: Keep the already-integrated pinned MIT YEIS destination model and existing React Navigator, then add only Personal Universe-specific grouping and lightweight ranking. This increases discoverability while retaining one astronomical index and one spatial authority.
decision.fallback: If result volume later makes lightweight ranking insufficient, add cmdk/Fuse only as a presentation/ranking layer over YEIS-resolved destinations rather than replacing YEIS search.
